query: For high-entropy alloys intended for thermal-insulation or radiation-resistant applications, what single intervention could reduce phonon thermal conductivity? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the physical mechanism, the predicted change relative to an otherwise comparable untreated alloy, the temperature and material-state boundaries over which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment whose result would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing lattice distortions through alloying can reduce phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Alloying with elements that introduce lattice distortions
generation.mechanism: Scattering of phonons by lattice distortions
generation.baseline: Untreated high-entropy alloy with no lattice distortions
generation.uncertainty: Effect of lattice distortions on phonon thermal conductivity at high temperatures

falsification_experiment.design: Measure phonon thermal conductivity of high-entropy alloys with and without lattice distortions at high temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If phonon thermal conductivity is not reduced in alloys with lattice distortions, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Gap and lever. Type: limitation. Statement: The study assumes the finite-temperature volume of the hcp structure is identical to that of the fcc structure, which is a simplification of the actual thermal expansion behavior.. System: CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy. Lever: hcp volume assumption. Quote: "In the present application, an ideal c / a ratio of 8/3 was employed for the hcp structure, the finite-temperature volume of which was assumed to be identical with the fcc one."

Gap and lever. Type: future_work. Statement: The authors suggest that future work should explicitly include phonon effects to improve the accuracy of phase stability predictions.. System: CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy. Lever: explicit phonon effect. Quote: "especially when taking into account the error bars stated in the experiments [16] and also the fact that the explicit phonon effect is not considered in the present theory."
